meta.title: Starbucks, Priced for the Comeback
meta.dek: Brian Niccol delivered a quarter that cleared every bar I set and guided fiscal 2027 EPS up 18%. The stock has gained 6% in two weeks. What does $104 assume about the margin that is still to come?
meta.price_note: Oct 30, 2026 close, matched on Yahoo Finance and StockAnalysis
meta.type: Global specialty-coffee retail, shifting from company-operated toward licensed

verdict.sentence: The margin turnaround is now proven and guided a year early, but at 32× next year's guide the price still assumes near-Bull margins; the probability-weighted case pays [[pw_return]] a year against the 13% hurdle.
verdict.breaks_if: Q1 FY2027 (late January) U.S. transactions turn negative against +3.0%, or the FY2027 guide of $3.15–3.25 is not reaffirmed, which would put the 13.5% margin out of reach.

call: Niccol cleared every bar I set: Q4 U.S. comps of +7.7% against a 6.5% guide, a non-GAAP operating margin of 14.0% against my 13%, fiscal 2026 EPS of $2.72 against a $2.55–2.65 guide, and a fiscal 2027 guide of $3.15–3.25 that puts the low end of the fiscal 2028 margin target a year early. The market is right that the margin walk is real. It is too generous on what is left to earn: Q4 transactions slowed to +2.4% from +4.2% and ticket (+5.2%) now does most of the work, the fiscal 2027 comp guide is about 4% with 'pricing well below CPI', and the 53rd week adds about ten cents of the $3.20. At $104 no Bear probability earns even an ordinary 9% a year; the price needs fiscal 2031 non-GAAP EPS of about [[Priced-in.eps]], close to our Bull. We give the Bear 25% because North America still earned a 12.0% GAAP margin for fiscal 2026 against 20.7% in fiscal 2023, and unit growth has been cut again (North America adds only 90–100 net new coffeehouses). The dividend is now covered, with about $1 billion of repurchases planned. Good business; the PW case returns [[pw_return]] and clears 13% only at [[entry]].

tests.claim: That the guided margin walk keeps going.
tests.test: on the Q1 FY2027 call (January 27), the FY2027 guide of EPS $3.15–3.25 and a 13.5–14.0% margin is reaffirmed and Q1 North America comps are at or above +4%.
tests.if_fail: Base FY2031 EPS cut to ≈$4.30 (PW EV [[test1.pw_ev]], [[test1.pw_return]]/yr) → stays **[[test1.verb]]**, entry [[test1.entry]].

tests.claim: That traffic survives the toughest compare.
tests.test: Q1 FY2027 (January 27) U.S. transactions positive against Q1 FY2026's +3.0%, with the two-year stack still above +1%. (The Q4 leg passed: +2.4%.)
tests.if_fail: move 10 points from Base to Bear (PW EV [[test2.pw_ev]], [[test2.pw_return]]/yr) → stays **[[test2.verb]]**, entry [[test2.entry]].

tests.claim: That owner earnings cover the dividend and the buyback.
tests.test: in the FY2026 10-K (mid-November), owner earnings ≥ the ~$2.8B dividend (the preliminary estimate is ≈$3.5B) and a disclosed uplift sales lift against control stores by the Q1 FY2027 print; the ≈$1B FY2027 buyback is funded without new debt.
tests.if_fail: move 10 points from Base to Bear (PW EV [[test3.pw_ev]], [[test3.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test3.verb]]**; the Outsider grade drops to Anti-Outsider for a dividend and buyback funded by debt.

return_math.epv: $26–35 per share (five-year owner earnings of $3.6B ÷ 9%; enterprise basis at the 15.5% median margin ≈$26). About two-thirds of the price pays for growth. The Bear ($67) sits well above EPV because it keeps ~4% growth and a 20× multiple; a no-growth Bear would be ≈$35.
return_math.base_rate: The Bull needs only ~5–6% nominal (~3% real) revenue growth, the FY2028 target; for companies above $25B, 31.8% reach 5% real growth over five years, so it is plausible. The constraint is margin, not sales.
return_math.year_ten: Still growing mid-single digits through licensed international stores and royalties; in the Bull the terminal multiple does much of the work.
